key_insight: LOKI discovers row-level join paths between disjoint tables by using text as evidence, turning implicit table-text links into explicit, typed integrations.
engineering_relevance: It helps data-lake systems integrate semantically related tables without predefined schemas, joins, or manual row-text supervision.
method: Horizontal bidirectional cross-attention encodes table rows and sentences in a shared latent space.
A global table-text contrastive objective learns fine-grained row-sentence associations without local labels.
Discovered associations are grouped into relation-consistent join paths and materialized as typed tables with sentence-level provenance.
evidence_signal: On real-world benchmarks, the approach outperforms multi-modal discovery baselines and reaches 0.982 macro typed-pair precision while using up to 40× less LLM API cost than direct prompting.
watch_item: Performance depends on reliable textual evidence and high-quality sentence retrieval, so noisy or sparse text may weaken discovered join paths.
paper_title: Discovery-Driven Integration of Disjoint Tables via Text
